maria: Quick heads-up — I pushed an update to the AWS Lambda quickstart auth snippet in PR #4321. Need a quick docs review for clarity + a small migration note for folks moving from SDK v4 -> v5.

sam: Thanks — what's the main UX change?

maria: Switched example from inline token var to using env var `REDWOOD_API_KEY` + added an explicit instruct to set the API region. Also simplified the handler to avoid streaming code (Lambda doesn't support streaming the same way).

jordan: Can you paste the new snippet here so I can skim?

maria: Sure — new snippet below (JS, Node 18):

```js
// handler.js
import fetch from 'node-fetch'
const API_KEY = process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY
export async function handler(event) {
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${API_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ input: event.body })
  })
  const data = await res.json()
  return { statusCode: 200, body: JSON.stringify(data) }
}
```

tina: tiny nit: in the PR description it's spelled "authntication" on line 2 — should be "authentication".

sam: I like the env var approach. We should call out: 1) where to set the env var in Lambda console, 2) the need to never check the key into source. Could add a one-liner migration note.

jordan: Also add a short sentence about cold-starts and that large models > 4k tokens may hit timeout — suggest testing locally and increasing timeout to 30s in the example.

maria: Good call. I'll add a 1‑liner on secrets and a short note about timeout/cold start.

docs-bot: Preview build for PR #4321: https://deploy-preview.redwood-docs/pr-4321 — build succeeded :white_check_mark: 

sam: I'll open a follow-up PR to fix the typo and add the Lambda console env var screenshot placeholder.

maria: Awesome — thanks y'all. If no other blockers I'll merge after the typo fix :rocket:
